first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent this as part of a reading pack on the wedding morning. The opening is calm and gets to the point, with no gushing and no prices, so I didn't close it. But it reads like a guide for a small bridal party with one hair person and one makeup artist and a friend keeping time. Useful logic, not written for a morning with a large family, several outfits and people who need privacy. I skimmed the rest, mainly the headings, the sample timeline and the Wedded Advisor lines.

journey.quote: A wedding morning timeline is built backwards from the ceremony: fix the time you leave, then the time you must be dressed, then when the photographer arrives, and start the first hair and makeup chair early enough to finish everyone before that.
journey.reaction: Sensible and plainly put. It doesn't oversell, which I like.

journey.section: The order of the hair and makeup chairs
journey.quote: With one stylist and one artist, two chairs run side by side: while one person is in hair, another is in makeup, then they swap.
journey.reaction: This is where I can tell it isn't for me. My mother, sisters, cousins and I would never be on one stylist and one artist. It assumes a small party.

journey.section: Stylists and artists for the number of people
journey.quote: If their answer starts earlier than anyone would like, the choice is an earlier start, or a second stylist or artist so more chairs run at once.
journey.reaction: 'A second stylist' is the most it imagines. For a big family morning I'd expect it at least to mention several teams or a second suite.

journey.section: Setting up the getting ready space
journey.quote: A friend who holds the schedule, calls the next person and keeps the room calm.
journey.reaction: I wouldn't hand this to a friend. It's a small thing, but it shows who the article pictures as its reader.

journey.section: Setting up the getting ready space
journey.quote: Room to work.** Space for two chairs, the kit, a rail for outfits and a corner where the photographer can step back.
journey.reaction: There's nothing here about who can come into the suite or whether anyone can photograph and post from it. On my wedding morning that's my first concern.

journey.quote: The suite or villa as base.** What time can you get in on the morning, and is there room for everyone, their outfits and the photographer?
journey.reaction: Good questions to ask a venue. This is the most relevant part for me, because the wedding will be abroad.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world and is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person.
journey.reaction: One person who handles everything is the right idea. But nothing on the page shows they've handled a wedding of my size, or that discretion is part of how they work.

journey.quote: Your partner's side needs its own timeline for grooming, dressing and photos.
journey.reaction: Fine as far as it goes. In our family the morning also has family moments and customs, and the article doesn't mention them at all.

journey.section: Plan the morning with one person
journey.quote: If you would like to plan it with someone, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Understated, and no package talk, which is good. 'Inclusions' sounds a little like a package. It's reassuring for a careful buyer but doesn't speak to me.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland planned weddings with 200 to 400 guests and a large family getting ready at the same time?
How does a Wedded Advisor handle privacy and confidentiality for a client's wedding (staff, vendors, photos, social media)?
Can the Advisor work with our own security team and our family office or assistant?
Is there a private way to make contact other than the general Wedded Concierge page?

turn_offs_found.quote: confirms inclusions in writing before you commit
turn_offs_found.why: 'Inclusions' is close to package language. It's mild, but it makes me feel like a standard client.

would_share_with: My assistant, to pass to whoever builds the run sheet for the morning

cta_reaction.why: Not from a how-to article. I'd only make contact through a referral or a private channel, and nothing here shows they work at my scale or with the discretion I need. My assistant might note the name.

top_3_changes: Acknowledge larger parties. Replace 'If their answer starts earlier than anyone would like, the choice is an earlier start, or a second stylist or artist so more chairs run at once.' with 'If their answer starts earlier than anyone would like, the choice is an earlier start, or more stylists and artists so more chairs run at once. For a large wedding party or several family members getting ready, ask whether a second room and team would keep the morning on time.'

Add privacy to the room set-up. Replace '- **One timekeeper.** A friend who holds the schedule, calls the next person and keeps the room calm.' with '- **Privacy.** Agree who may enter the suite, and whether anyone may photograph or post from it.
- **One timekeeper.** A friend or a member of your team who holds the schedule, calls the next person and keeps the room calm.'

Make room for family customs without stereotyping. Replace 'Hand the rings to a named person early.' with 'Hand the rings to a named person early. If your families have customs, blessings or quiet moments on the morning, give each its own block on the timeline.'

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, assistant reads first, referral-led)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored

Suggested edits are exact old/new strings with no prices, statistics, durations as fact, 'free', 'last dance', vendor names, fees, on-the-ground claims, transfers, room blocks, availability, or implication that the Advisor runs the morning
Payload matches 07-icp schema (scores 1 to 5, max 3 top changes)
